comments.author: 9f144030-5747-41ee-a3f6-f03a838c088c
comments.comment: The cleanest approach is a recursive solution. At each node, compare the value to insert against the current node's value. If smaller, recurse into the left subtree; if larger, recurse into the right subtree. When you reach a null node, that is where the new value belongs - create and return a new Node there. The recursion unwinds and re-links the tree automatically.
comments.title: Recursive Insert Solution

sections.description: Base case: if root is null, return a new Node. Recursive case: compare val to root.val and recurse left or right.
sections.title: Recursive Implementation

comments.author: 9f144030-5747-41ee-a3f6-f03a838c088c
comments.comment: An iterative approach avoids recursion stack overhead, which matters for very deep or unbalanced trees. Start at the root and walk down the tree using a pointer. At each step, decide to go left or right based on the comparison. Keep track of the parent node so you can attach the new node once you reach a null slot. This is O(h) time where h is the height of the tree.
comments.title: Iterative Insert Solution

description: A Binary Search Tree (BST) is a node-based data structure where each node has a key greater than all keys in its left subtree and less than all keys in its right subtree. Your task is to implement the insert operation for a BST. Given the root of an existing BST and an integer value, insert the value into the correct position while maintaining the BST property. You must handle the case where the tree is empty (root is null). Return the root of the modified tree.
title: Binary Search Tree Implementation

comments.author: 9f144030-5747-41ee-a3f6-f03a838c088c
comments.comment: Each traversal is a simple recursive function. The key insight is that the only difference between them is the position of the 'process current node' step relative to the recursive calls. In-order processes the node between the two recursive calls, making it ideal for retrieving BST values in sorted order. Pre-order processes the node first (useful for copying/serialising a tree). Post-order processes the node last (useful for deletion, since you delete children before the parent).
comments.title: All Three Traversals Implemented

author: 9f144030-5747-41ee-a3f6-f03a838c088c
hints: In-order traversal of a BST always visits nodes in sorted order. Why?
The only difference between the three traversals is when you visit the current node.
All three traversals have the same O(n) time complexity - every node is visited exactly once.
Think about which traversal you would use to make a copy of the tree.
description: Tree traversal is the process of visiting every node in a tree exactly once. For a Binary Search Tree there are three standard depth-first traversal orders: in-order (left -> root -> right), pre-order (root -> left -> right), and post-order (left -> right -> root). In-order traversal of a BST always produces the node values in sorted ascending order, which is one of its most useful properties. Implement all three traversals for a BST and explain when you would choose each one.
title: Binary Search Tree Traversal
